news.text: 4 July saw the bloody debut of **WarGames: The Match Beyond** at The Omni in Atlanta during the NWA Great American Bash. Conceived by Dusty Rhodes, the brutal double-ring, enclosed steel-cage war saw Team Dusty (Rhodes, Nikita Koloff, The Road Warriors, and Paul Ellering) triumph over The Four Horsemen when manager J.J. Dillon submitted to horrific agony. The match left ring canvas soaked in crimson, immediately cementing WarGames as one of the most genuinely punishing innovations in professional wrestling history.

news.text: 11 July saw the United Nations calculate that the global human population had surpassed five billion people, marked officially as the **Day of Five Billion**. The demographic milestone was symbolically personified by the birth of baby Matej Gaspar in Zagreb, Yugoslavia, triggering intense international debate regarding planetary resources and urban growth. Sociologists pointed out that global headcount had doubled in just under four decades, while wry commentators wondered if Earth was quietly running out of patio space.

news.text: 15 July saw President Chiang Ching-kuo officially lift **martial law in Taiwan**, terminating an astonishing 38 continuous years of military decree. Enacted back in May 1949 during the Chinese Civil War, the emergency legislation had banned opposition political parties, tightly censored domestic newspapers and curbed civil assemblies. The historic repeal cleared the path for democratic multiparty governance, sparking Taiwan's rapid rise into one of East Asia's most progressive technological and economic powerhouses.

news.text: 17 July saw Paul Verhoeven's blistering dystopian thriller *RoboCop* blast into North American cinemas, delivering a savage satire of Reagan-era corporate excess wrapped in visceral cyberpunk action. Starring **Peter Weller** as murdered Detroit police officer Alex Murphy, reconstructed by Omni Consumer Products as an indestructible cyborg lawman, the movie shocked critics with its razor-sharp wit and outrageous faux advertisements. Audiences cheered Murphy's tragic redemption and his cold ultimatum: "Dead or alive, you're coming with me."

news.text: 19 July saw pop queen **Madonna** claim the UK singles chart summit once more as *Who's That Girl* climbed to number one, knocking the Pet Shop Boys' *It's a Sin* off the top perch. Serving as the title theme for her upcoming screwball cinema vehicle, the upbeat Latin-pop track marked the superstar's fifth UK number-one single in just two years. While the accompanying motion picture would soon be shredded by cinematic reviewers, the infectious single ensured Madonna's radio supremacy was entirely untroubled by poor box-office receipts.

news.text: 24 July saw Elite Systems' celebrated arcade conversion *Paperboy* secure the number one spot on the UK Gallup software charts, buoyed by strong home micro sales across the **Commodore 64** and **ZX Spectrum**. Dodging rogue lawnmowers, wayward dogs and unhinged breakdancers, players pedalled frantically through American suburbia while delivering newspapers to daily subscribers and smashing windows of non-subscribers. The port proved that cycling around a paper round on an 8-bit home micro was infinitely more lethal than doing the real job.

31 July saw deadly violence shake the holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia, when an anti-Western demonstration by Iranian pilgrims escalated into bloody clashes with Saudi security personnel. Over 400 people were killed in the ensuing gunfire and catastrophic crowd crushes, leading to an immediate breakdown of diplomatic ties between Riyadh and Tehran. The grim tragedy sparked furious protests throughout the Muslim world, severely escalating sectarian and geopolitical tensions amid the bloody climax of the Iran-Iraq War.
